verified_context: A peer-reviewed study reports that DynaVelo nominated Ctcf, Bcl6 and Stat3 perturbations to rescue an Arid1a-loss phenotype in murine germinal-center B cells. Same-team mouse experiments restored the studied dark-zone/light-zone ratio for all three; this is preclinical evidence in one system, not a therapy or patient outcome.
visual_idea: A staged, cinematic macro photograph of a researcher's gloved hands arranging three distinct translucent glass markers along three physical branching paths on a warm backlit laboratory light table, with the paths converging toward one softly illuminated circular glass dish. The tactile three-path composition represents three model-nominated perturbations followed into laboratory tests without depicting an actual biological mechanism, dataset or study apparatus.
constraints: Selected from three written concepts. Chosen concept: the three-path light-table still life makes the model-to-experiment relationship specific and legible at 160px while avoiding another clinician-at-monitor scene. Rejected concept 1: a researcher facing a multiomic network on a monitor would repeat two recent workstation compositions and risk fabricated scientific graphics. Rejected concept 2: a mouse-facility portrait with three cages could imply documentary access to the reported experiments and turn animals into a sensational focal point. Create one standalone 3:2 photorealistic editorial science photograph, not an illustration, diagram, collage, card or screenshot. Meaningful human presence is limited to anonymous gloved hands actively choosing among three physical paths. Use believable optical glass pieces, shallow depth of field, directional amber-and-neutral laboratory light, tactile bench texture and a crop-safe focal relationship between the three markers and their converging paths. Keep all three branches and the hands legible in 16:9 and mobile object-fit crops. The scene must read as an openly staged metaphor, not the authors, institution, reported experiment, actual B cells, a gene network, a treatment or a measured result. No mouse, patient, clinician, monitor, interface, readable text, letters, numbers, labels, charts, molecular structures, DNA helix, glowing brain, robot, logo, institutional identifier, product, syringe, drug, approval cue, border, frame or watermark.
